body.statement: If \(Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,Gamma)=1\), then the digest binds \(Gamma\) to that complete fixed instance and those serialized groundings; \(Ictx\) is the exact source and target incidence table; \(K\) consists exactly of the target-relevant rows recovered from positive source parent contexts; \(rstar\) is the unique unsupported target-relevant row; and replay of the target factorization yields \(F\). The root records enumerate every point in \(Ccrit\), every candidate-to-value link is correct, \(L=\min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)\), and \(U=\max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)\). Decoding \(Z\) yields \(Mminus,Mplus\in Mone\), exact reproduction of \(Psrc\), and \(Q(Mminus)=L\), \(Q(Mplus)=U\). These conclusions remain valid with repeated derivative roots, boundary critical points, equal candidate values, boundary ties, algebraic conjugates, and threshold coincidences.
body.justification: Soundness turns an untrusted producer's output into an independently checkable causal claim.
body.gap: Li, Passmore, and Paulson and Narkawicz, Mu\~noz, and Dutle verify univariate formulas; neither composes those checks with relational factorization and source-compatible endpoint models.
body.consumer: A rejected conjugate or omitted positive critical point cannot silently alter the reported N3 range.
body.proof_tex:
Assume
\[
 Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,\rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,\Gamma)=1.
\]
By the definition of \(Check\), every guarded check in
\(\texttt{def:checker}\) has returned true.  We show successively what
those checks imply.

First, the checker recomputes the injective, length-delimited canonical
digest from the supplied fixed instance and \(Z\).  Equality with the
digest stored in \(\Gamma\) therefore gives equality of the entire encoded
tuples, rather than merely equality of an ambiguous concatenation.  The
schema-reference, edge-reference, lexicographic-index, and acyclicity
checks then show that the accepted \(Ictx\) has one and only one record
for every required source ground node and every event-consistent complete
target-assignment term of the supplied groundings, with the recorded
context, parent tuple, intervention status, and target-relevance flag.
Thus it is their exact incidence table.

For a row claimed to be supported, the checker recomputes its source
parent-context probability and checks that this rational number is
strictly positive before division.  It then divides the corresponding
joint cells by that positive number and compares every result with the
row recorded in \(K\).  Hence all such divisions are defined and \(K\)
contains exactly the recovered target-relevant positive-support rows.
Equality checks between occurrences with the same type--context label
enforce type sharing.  Exhaustiveness of the relevance records, followed
by the source-support checks, leaves exactly the recorded key \(rstar\)
unsupported.  Finally, each rational addition and multiplication in the
truncated-factorization replay is checked, and the terminal dense
coefficient list is compared coefficient by coefficient with \(F\).
Therefore the supplied polynomial is exactly the causal replay polynomial.

We next analyze the algebraic portion.  The checker verifies an integer
clearing of \(F'\), its gcd data, and its square-free part \(g\).  In the
constant and nonzero-constant-derivative cases it uses the designated
boundary-only record.  Otherwise,
\(\texttt{lem:sturm-root-count-correctness}\) implies that an accepted
rational interval of Sturm count one contains exactly one distinct real
root of \(g\), an interval of count zero contains none, and the checked
variation counts over the disjoint subdivision account for every root.
The feasibility signs retain exactly the roots in \((0,1)\), while the
separate boundary records account for \(0\) and \(1\).  Since a polynomial
and its square-free part have the same distinct roots, repeated roots of
\(F'\) are represented once.  Hence the accepted candidate list is
exactly \(Ccrit\), including all boundary cases.

Fix a listed candidate \(c\).  For an interior candidate, \(g(c)=0\).
In the Sylvester determinant defining that resultant, specialization at
\(z=F(c)\) makes the two input polynomials share the root \(c\), so the
corresponding evaluation matrix has a nonzero kernel and its determinant
vanishes.  The checked resultant identity therefore implies that \(F(c)\)
is a root of the associated value polynomial; for a boundary candidate, exact
rational substitution gives the corresponding assertion.  A resultant
alone could include conjugate or infeasible values, so the checker also
verifies the candidate-specific Sturm--Tarski signs.  If
\(J=(\ell,u)\) is the one-root rational isolator carrying the proposed
value label, those accepted signs give
\[
 \ell<F(c)<u.
\]
The root-count check says that \(J\) contains exactly one root of the
square-free value polynomial.  Thus the linked algebraic number is
necessarily \(F(c)\), not an unrelated conjugate root of the resultant.

The exact sign comparisons totally order distinct value labels.  The
checker assigns a common tie label precisely when the candidate-specific
algebraic equality test succeeds; otherwise disjoint one-root isolators
and strict sign comparisons determine the order.  Therefore equal
interior values, boundary ties, and boundary--interior coincidences are
handled without an invalid numerical separation step.  The selected least
and greatest labels satisfy
\[
 L=\min_{c\in Ccrit}F(c),\qquad
 U=\max_{c\in Ccrit}F(c).
\]
By the critical-point argument in \(\texttt{thm:sharp-one-row}\), these
are also
\[
 L=\min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q),\qquad
 U=\max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q).
\]
An algebraic root having no link from a feasible candidate cannot be
selected.  The same exact sign mechanism checks all
rational-versus-algebraic threshold comparisons, including equality.

Finally, decode \(Z\).  The accepted nonnegativity signs and exact
unit-sum identities make every listed finite-noise table a probability
law.  Shared table labels give one mechanism per endogenous type, and the
node-copy records give mutually independent noise draws at distinct ground
nodes.  The mechanism-output, graph-reference, and incidence checks place
each output in the supplied context and grounding.  Summing the checked
atom masses over output labels recovers every conditional row.  The source
evaluation records multiply these rows in a topological order and agree
cell by cell with \(Psrc\); the positivity checks used above justify every
conditional recovery.  The target records omit exactly the intervened
factors, sum every event-consistent term in \(Ictx\), and agree exactly
with \(L\) and \(U\).  Thus the two decoded models satisfy every clause of
\(\texttt{def:model-class}\), reproduce \(Psrc\), and obey
\[
 Mminus,Mplus\in Mone,\qquad
 Q(Mminus)=L,\qquad Q(Mplus)=U.
\]
All implications used exact identities or certified signs, so repeated
derivative roots, boundary critical points, equal values, algebraic
conjugates, and threshold coincidences do not change the conclusion.
